Why join CalHR?

The California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) is the pillar of human resources management for all state employees. Our success is made possible by the hard work of more than 400 CalHR team members who serve as trusted advisors to our strategic partners and the public. If you are interested in providing exceptional human resource services and guidance, CalHR is the place for you. By joining our team, you’ll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while working alongside passionate professionals. Get to know us more here!

CalHR employees are excluded from bargaining and are eligible to receive enhanced benefits, such as CoBen benefit allowance, employer paid life insurance, additional vacation/annual leave, and are not subject to State Disability Insurance payroll withholding.

About This Role

Are you passionate about Human Resources (HR)? Do others look to you as an HR leader? Are you interested in making civil service HR better? Do you want to work with a diverse, dedicated team of experts to provide statewide policy guidance and customer support to the HR community? Then the Personnel Management Division (PMD) may be the right home for you. As a leader in the management team within PMD, you will oversee the day to day administrative activities of a team of personnel professionals, provide classification and compensation policy guidance to departments and agencies and address complex statewide personnel management issues in collaboration with other managers and stakeholders. If you can't resist an HR mystery or a challenge, apply for PMD today!

As a key member and a recognized statewide authority of the Personnel Management Division, this position is distinguished from other division managers because of its greater complexity and sensitivity of assigned responsibilities with Exempt and Career Executive Assignment (CEA) appointments in a Control Agency setting. Under the general direction of the Assistant Division Chief (CEA), the incumbent is responsible for managing the day-to-day activities of a team of personnel professionals within the division; serves as a point of contact with the Governor's Office on Exempt appointments and Executive salaries; serves as the primary contact for the CEA salary program; and serves as an assistant Secretary for the California Citizens Compensation Commission;. The incumbent provides high-level management advice and determinations to the Governor's Office and Executives in State service.

If you are as passionate about helping those in need as you are about growing your career, consider AltaMed. At AltaMed, your passion for helping others isn’t just welcomed – it’s nurtured, celebrated, and promoted, allowing you to grow while making a meaningful difference. We don’t just serve our communities; we are an integral part of them. By raising the expectations of what a community clinic can deliver, we demonstrate our belief that quality care is for everyone. Our commitment to providing exceptional care, despite any challenges, goes beyond just a job; it’s a calling that drives us forward every day.

Job Overview

The Community Health Workers (CHW) are trusted members of their community who help address chronic conditions, preventive health care needs, and health-related social needs. CHWs have the skills and experience to understand what at-risk or vulnerable patients are going through and help them get through difficult times. CHWs help patients address the social, medical, and community problems that lead to poor health. The goal is to help patients address real-life obstacles (e.g., social driver of health) that keep them from staying healthy, by supporting them with health care navigation, specialty appointments/referrals, PCP appointments/establishing routine care and preventative health screenings, cultural broker, financial services, and provide culturally appropriate health information on topics related to chronic disease management and prevention. CHWs receive training in Epic & Essette, DHCS requirements, trauma-informed care, motivational interviewing, health care navigation, harm reduction, mental health first aid, domestic/intimate partner violence, advocacy, insurance enrollment, social service/resource applications and referrals, and basic case management.

jobs.description:
For nearly 20 years, TheKey has helped clients achieve successful long-term aging at home with comprehensive, concierge-based care. Ensuring the dignity, safety, and independence of its clients, TheKey is committed to changing how the world lives and ages at home. Employee-teams get the training, resources, and support they need to deliver an exceptional care experience for clients and their families. Founded in Silicon Valley, TheKey has grown from a single location to service coverage throughout North America enabling clients to live life on their own terms, in their own homes.

Who We Are

TheKey is led by a team that reflects a wide range of industry experience in home care, senior care, and healthcare, along with deep expertise in technology, operations, transformation, and customer experience. This includes guidance from our Scientific Advisory Board, made up of nine experts in brain health, aging, and geriatrics, alongside the day-to-day expertise of our clinical and care teams who bring this work to life in the home. But what unites everyone at TheKey, from our leadership team to our caregivers, is a shared passion for reimagining what aging at home can look like. We're driven by a common mission: helping more older adults get the services and tools they need to age well, where and how they want.

The Role

The Client Care Manager oversees a group of clients with varying needs and hours. This role is responsible for partnering with clients, families, and medical professionals to design tailored service plans. You will also be responsible for the selection, guidance, and supervision of the Caregiver teams assigned to implement these plans, making adjustments as needed to maintain high levels of client satisfaction and retention. This role is an integral part of the site’s performance and success.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate would be someone who has a scheduling, care coordination, or Client Management background. We are looking for an individual with experience in health care, elder care, social work, or a related industry. Because our client’s needs can shift often, we desire someone who has the foresight to resolve potential problems before they arise and can proactively identify areas of interest prior to initial meetings. Must have exceptional communication skills, a high level of emotional intelligence, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment where managing complex family dynamics is required. Candidates are expected to leverage AI tools strategically and responsibly to enhance efficiency, improve client outcomes, and support data-informed decision-making. We value individuals who can identify where technology adds meaningful value while maintaining the human-centered approach that is at the heart of everything we do at TheKey. And lastly, we seek someone who finds fulfillment in making a meaningful, daily impact on the lives of others, ensuring the dignity and independence of seniors through a holistic, person-centered approach.

Client Care Manager Duties And Responsibilities

Oversee day-to-day client relationships and the delivery of high-quality, holistic care tailored to individual needs.
Conduct assessments with prospective clients to design service plans and build rapport with families.
Manage and supervise caregiver teams, ensuring care plans are documented, updated, and effectively implemented.
Proactively communicate with internal and external stakeholders to evaluate solutions and ensure client satisfaction.
Handle escalations, ensure regulatory compliance, and identify opportunities to grow the business through quality service.
Manage the Start of Care process to ensure high-quality experiences and complete satisfaction for new clients.
Conduct in-person re-assessments and quality assurance visits to evaluate home safety, daily routines, and evolving client needs.

Required Skills, Education, And Certifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Human or Health Services or a related profession from an accredited university preferred, or equivalent work experience
3 years experience in health care, elder care, social work, or related industry preferred
Excellent customer service and conflict resolution skills
Computer proficiency and EMR experience
Current driver’s license and proof of insurance

Requires the ability to travel locally up to 75% of the time, lift and carry up to 20 pounds, stand or walk for prolonged periods, and use standard office equipment.

At IBM Software, we transform client challenges into solutions. Building the world’s leading AI-powered, cloud-native products that shape the future of business and society. Confluent is looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help lead complex, cross-functional initiatives across the Business Technology / CIO organization. This role sits at the intersection of Product, Engineering, and enterprise systems, turning strategic priorities into executable plans and measurable outcomes.

The Senior TPM will play a critical role in driving enterprise programs that support new product introductions, Quote-to-Cash capabilities, and major IT integration efforts. Because Business Technology owns core downstream systems that enable Product and Engineering launches, this person will help ensure programs are planned well, dependencies are surfaced early, and delivery stays predictable across a broad set of stakeholders.

This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who is comfortable navigating ambiguity, aligning technical and business teams, and driving execution across multiple workstreams. The ideal candidate combines strong program leadership, technical fluency, operational discipline, and stakeholder management skills to help teams deliver scalable and reliable outcomes.

Lead large, complex, cross-functional programs from planning through execution and delivery.
Partner with Business Technology, Product, Engineering, and operational teams to define scope, clarify business value, and translate goals into structured roadmaps.
Drive programs supporting new product introductions (NPI), especially where Quote-to-Cash systems and enterprise platforms are critical downstream dependencies.
Coordinate initiatives involving enterprise applications and IT systems integrations, including support for integration efforts tied to IBM and other strategic business changes.
Build and maintain integrated program plans, timelines, milestones, and communication rhythms across multiple teams and functions.
Identify risks, dependencies, blockers, and trade-offs early, and drive clear decision-making to keep programs on track.
Create visibility for stakeholders and leadership through consistent status updates, execution dashboards, and clear reporting on progress, issues, and outcomes.
Partner with teams to improve delivery predictability, execution rigor, and operational readiness across programs.

7+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Program Management, or related roles within software, SaaS, or enterprise systems environments.
Proven track record delivering large-scale, cross-functional programs, managing multiple stakeholders, risks, dependencies, and parallel initiatives.
Strong expertise in Agile program management tools and practices, including Jira for workflow management, tracking deliverables, and reporting progress.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence outcomes and build alignment across technical, operational, and executive audiences in a matrixed organization.
Highly collaborative and execution-focused, with strong attention to detail, experience working with globally distributed teams, and a bias for action in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
